topic: Object Memory Layout and Data Member Arrangement in Inheritance Hierarchies
explanation: This concept explains how C++ compilers organize data members within objects in memory, especially considering inheritance structures. It details how data members are laid out to ensure correct access, alignment, and efficiency, including how base and derived class members are arranged in memory. Understanding this internal layout is crucial for grasping object size, offset calculations, and the impact of inheritance models (single, multiple, virtual) on memory organization.
book: Inside the C++ Object Model by Stanley B. Lippman
